content: Binding the persistence entity directly to the request body with no `@Valid`/whitelist means every writable column is client-controlled (mass assignment): the caller can pass `id`, `status`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` on create/update. Setting `status` lets a caller create a config that is invisible to `list()` (which filters `status=1`) or resurrect/soft-delete a config, bypassing the dedicated delete endpoint. Consider a request DTO exposing only the editable fields (flowName/flowType/approverType/approverIds/signMode/sortOrder) and validating it with `@Valid`, so `status`/`id`/audit timestamps stay server-controlled.

The update returns `Result.ok()` unconditionally. Since the service calls `configMapper.updateById(config)`, which silently affects 0 rows when the id does not exist (or was already soft-deleted), a caller updating a bogus id gets a success response while nothing changed. Recommend verifying the record exists (e.g., `getById`/affected-rows from the service) and returning a not-found error to avoid false-positive success.

The result order is the sole determinant of the serial stage sequence (see `ApprovalConfigService.createNodes`, which assigns `nodeOrder` from the list index and relies on "config 按 sort_order 即串行阶段序"). `ORDER BY sort_order` alone is non-deterministic when several configs share the same sort_order, so different executions of the same approval flow can produce different stage ordering. Add a tie-breaker column.

content: Off-by-one against the row limit: `rowNum` is a 1-based **Excel row number** (header = row 1, first data row = 2), while `ImportGuard.checkRow` / `MAX_IMPORT_ROWS` is defined as a **data-row count** limit. With N data rows the guard receives N+1, so a file with exactly 5000 data rows is rejected with "导入数据超过 5000 行上限". Additionally, a manually incremented counter can drift from the real Excel row when EasyExcel skips blank rows, which would also mis-report the row number in `FailDetail`. Suggest deriving the row number from the analysis context and passing a data-row count to the guard.

Database query issued per row inside the read loop: `existsByName` performs a scoped `selectCount` (up to `MAX_IMPORT_ROWS` times) and `customerService.create(...)` then does several more statements per row — the classic N+1 pattern. For a 5000-row file this is thousands of round-trips while the HTTP request is held open. Consider pre-loading the existing names for the current scope into a `Set` with a single query (and relying on the DB unique constraint as the final guard), or batch-load/batch-insert, plus in-memory de-duplication of names within the same file.

The upper bound is clamped but the lower bound is not: a client can pass `detailLimit` as a negative value (e.g. `?detailLimit=-1`). In `FileReconciliationService.reconcile` the guard is `missingList.size() < detailLimit`, so a negative limit silently produces zero `missingDetail` entries, and an audit/治理 endpoint silently returns an empty missing list — misleading for an admin operation. content: Check-then-act race: `fileExists` only checks existence and the subsequent `Files.copy(... REPLACE_EXISTING)` / `ossClient.putObject` blindly overwrites. Two concurrent uploads of the same name in the same scope/user directory can resolve to the same `fileKey`; the second write silently overwrites the first, leaving two `BizFile` rows pointing at one object — deleting either one physically removes the other's content. Generate the unique segment atomically (UUID/timestamp) or create the local file with `StandardCopyOption` exclusion / use a per-directory lock, and re-check the OSS key with a conditional put (`x-oss-forbid-overwrite`).

The thumbnail response of an authorization-protected download endpoint is marked `public`, allowing shared caches/proxies/CDN to store and re-serve the bytes without re-running `canDownloadFile`. Use a private cache policy (`private, max-age=3600`) or drop Cache-Control for these authorized responses.

Uploading e.g. `scope=private` into a public folder (or `scope=public` into a private folder, which the owner is allowed to do) stores a file whose `fileScope` never matches the folder type used by `pageFiles`' visibility filter, so the file becomes invisible/undeletable in both tabs while still consuming the uploader's private quota. Inconsistent with the rest of the project: every other entity (BaseEntity, BizInvoice, BizCustomer, ...) annotates `createdAt`/`updatedAt` with `@TableField(fill = FieldFill.INSERT)` / `@TableField(fill = FieldFill.INSERT_UPDATE)`, and a `MetaObjectHandler` is registered in `MybatisPlusConfig`. Here the fields have no fill annotation, and neither `ReminderService.generateExpiringReminders()` nor `CustomerExpireTask` sets them, so the values depend entirely on the MySQL column defaults (`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`). If the schema default is ever missing/overridden (e.g. H2 test schema, or a table created without DEFAULT), the inserted rows get `createdAt = null`, and the de-duplication query `ge(BizReminder::getCreatedAt, todayStart).lt(..., todayEnd)` as well as `orderByDesc(BizReminder::getCreatedAt)` will silently misbehave (duplicate reminders / undefined ordering). `Long::parseLong` is unguarded: any malformed id in the CSV (e.g. a trailing separator, "null", or non-numeric input produced by an import/manual DB edit) throws `NumberFormatException`, which surfaces as a 500 error rather than a clean validation failure — and this parser is used by the save/delete path via `checkOfficeOverlap`. Consider filtering non-numeric tokens or wrapping the parse and raising a `BusinessException`.

`size` (and `current`) are taken straight from the request and passed to `new Page<>(current, size)` without any upper bound; `PaginationInnerInterceptor` is registered without `setMaxLimit`, so a client can request an arbitrarily large page (or a negative size, which MyBatis-Plus treats as "no pagination") and force the server to materialise the whole reminder table — a cheap resource-exhaustion vector.
